replacements.new:
Life insurance for a specific situation

Some needs raise their own questions, so each one has its own page:

  • A home loan. Mortgage protection insurance is usually term life that you own, sized to what you owe and the years left on the loan. It is not the mortgage insurance a lender may ask for.
  • Military service. If you have or had SGLI, VGLI or VALife, life insurance for veterans sets VA coverage next to private policies. Honorbrook is an independent agency and is not part of the VA.
  • A child or grandchild. A child rider on a parent's policy is one way to cover a child, and a separate policy on the child is another. Children's life insurance compares the two.
  • An estate or a business. Life insurance for high-net-worth families explains how coverage is used for estate costs, business succession and heirs. It is general education, not tax advice.

Life insurance by state

If you have children, an add-on to know about is the child rider. Virginia's Bureau of Insurance says spousal or family riders give you the option of buying life insurance on your spouse or children. How much you can buy depends on the company's underwriting limits, and riders usually add to the premium (Virginia Consumer's Guide for Life Insurance, page last updated January 5, 2024). What a rider covers varies by carrier and state. Our children's life insurance page compares a rider on your own policy with a separate policy on the child.

Served in the military? VGLI, which VA offers after you leave the service, is also term life insurance. VA bases its rates on your age and the amount of coverage (VA.gov: VGLI, updated October 13, 2026). A private term policy is also priced on your health. Our life insurance for veterans page explains how VGLI and a private term policy differ.

No-exam and accelerated underwriting

replacements.old: When something else is the better answer
replacements.new:
For veterans and people leaving the service: VA says SGLI and VGLI can each be converted to an individual policy from a participating company. The new policy has to be permanent coverage, such as whole life (VA.gov: SGLI, updated November 19, 2026; VA.gov: VGLI, updated October 13, 2026). Converting is one choice among several. Our life insurance for veterans page lists VA's deadlines and the other options to compare.

When something else is the better answer
replacements.why: Links /veterans-life-insurance with the one VA fact that belongs on a whole life page: SGLI and VGLI convert only to permanent policies. Sources (va.gov only): https://www.va.gov/life-insurance/options-eligibility/vgli/ (Last updated October 13, 2026): "The conversion policy must be a permanent policy, such as a whole life policy." https://www.va.gov/life-insurance/options-eligibility/sgli/ (Last updated November 19, 2026): "convert your SGLI coverage to a permanent, individual insurance policy (like whole life)". Says converting is one choice among several, so it is not a push to convert. This page already links the high-net-worth page in its body, so no second link was added. CHECKER (Nov 25, 2026), reworded: "VA lets you convert" now reads "VA says ... can each be converted to an individual policy from a participating company". VA's pages say a conversion goes through the companies on VA's list, so the sentence no longer reads as if VA, or this agency, issues the new policy. "Service members" became "people leaving the service" because VA ties the SGLI conversion to leaving the military. Split the 40-word sentence. Both VA quotes and both page dates match va.gov.
